subject: Request: provisional SLA coverage waiver + monthly offset schedule
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver@starlite.co>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@starlite.co>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary coverage ask — impact on uptime commitment and monthly offset

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Starlite is excited about Redwood's latency profile for our batch and streaming jobs. Before we move to contract, our compliance and ops teams raised a short-term concern: during our planned data migration (late Q3) we anticipate a predictable but material uptick in traffic that will temporarily raise latency and increase error rates on a small subset of endpoints.

Because our release timeline is tight, we are asking whether Redwood can (a) permit a provisional waiver of the standard 99.95% per-month uptime requirement for the migration month, and (b) accept a fixed monthly offset (service credit schedule) tied to measured degradation rather than the usual remedy ladder.

High-level ask: 1) Reduce guaranteed uptime floor from 99.95% to 99.5% for month-of-migration (September), 2) Cap monthly credit at a fixed offset ($8k) to simplify procurement, 3) Provide a lightweight monitoring/alerting snapshot during the migration window so our SREs and Redwood ops can collaborate in real time.

We can move quickly — procurement and legal want a short addendum rather than full SLA redline. Attaching our internal migration timeline (not attached here). What do you think?

Best,
Oliver
Operations Lead, Starlite Systems
[Attachment: migration-timeline.csv (referenced)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver@starlite.co>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary coverage ask — impact on uptime commitment and monthly offset

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear summary.

We can support a short-lived, documented exception but want to ensure the mechanism is safe for both sides. Quick take: we can allow a one-month provisional uptime floor adjustment (99.95% -> 99.50%) with an explicit carveout window and predefined rollback conditions. In lieu of the normal tiered remedy ladder, we can agree to a fixed monthly offset — but would propose $7,500 rather than $8,000 to keep parity with expected token spend during the migration.

Operational asks from our side:
- A fixed migration window (start/end timestamps) so our routing and capacity teams can schedule extra buffer;
- An SRE contact list and Slack channel for the window;
- Post-migration health check and a short RCA if degradation exceeds the waiver scope.

I'll loop in Ben to formalize the offset language and attach a short addendum draft. How fast do you need the doc?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Oliver Park <oliver@starlite.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary coverage ask — impact on uptime commitment and monthly offset

Oliver / team — appreciate the heads-up and the migration details in the demo notes. A couple of legal/ops clarifications from our side before we lock numbers:

1) Carveout scope: we need to list the specific endpoints and model routes that will be exempted. Please share the route list (API paths and model names).
2) Measurement: remediation/offset will be tied to our production monitoring (per-route availability and p95 latency). We propose using the same measurement window you use to validate your migration progress to avoid double-counting.
3) Duration & rollback: propose a maximum one calendar month waiver. If the migration takes longer, we revert to standard SLA and discuss a phased extension.

We can accept $7,500 fixed offset if Starlite agrees the waiver applies only to the named endpoints and you confirm a migration start/end. Ben — please draft addendum language that captures the fixed-offset schedule and monitoring hooks. Marissa — can you prep the addendum template and attach the offset table?

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal & Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver@starlite.co>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary coverage ask — impact on uptime commitment and monthly offset

Oliver — attaching a short addendum draft and an offset table for your procurement team to review. Key points in the draft:
- Waiver scope: named endpoints (you can add model/route list in the appendix)
- Waiver period: Sept 15 00:00 PDT -> Oct 15 00:00 PDT (one month) — flexible to adjust to your exact migration window
- Fixed monthly offset: $7,500 payable as a billing credit applied to the Oct invoice if measured availability for the named endpoints falls below 99.5% during the waiver period
- Monitoring: Redwood will provide a live readout via a shared Slack channel and a short daily snapshot during the window
- Rollback: automatic rollback to standard SLA after the period; any extension requires mutual written agreement

Attachments: [Attachment: SLA-offset-proposal.pdf (PDF, 42KB)], [Attachment: monthly-offset-table.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)]

Please review and confirm whether procurement/legal at Starlite are comfortable with the $7.5k cap and the measurement approach. Happy to iterate.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Park <oliver@starlite.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@starlite.co>, Legal <legal@starlite.co>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary coverage ask — impact on uptime commitment and monthly offset

Thanks Ben / Vivek / Laura — the draft looks reasonable and the $7.5k cap is acceptable to procurement (I confirmed with our buyer). A few small asks from our side before we sign:
- Replace the word "automatic rollback" with "automatic reinstatement of standard SLA" to be explicit;
- Add a one-week post-migration validation window so we can jointly verify metrics and close the incident scope;
- Include a single line in the appendix listing the three endpoints to be covered (we'll send that by EOD Friday).

If you can incorporate those tweaks, legal will route the addendum for signature and procurement will create the PO. Thanks for moving quickly on this.

Oliver
Operations Lead, Starlite Systems
